event_description: Executive Order 32: mandatory water conservation measures during the 2002 statewide drought, the drought emergency later ended by Executive Order 34.
Limited State of Emergency for a winter storm with heavy snow in Kent and Sussex counties.
State of Emergency for Hurricane Irene, with coastal flooding and wind expected in Sussex County.
Limited State of Emergency and mandatory evacuation of the areas most at risk for Hurricane Sandy, strengthened statewide October 28.
State of Emergency for a winter storm with heavy snow.
State of Emergency in Kent and New Castle counties for a winter storm with snow, sleet and wind.
State of Emergency and Level 1 Driving Warning for a winter storm with snow.
Limited State of Emergency in Sussex County for high winds and coastal flooding from a nor'easter and Hurricane Joaquin.
State of Emergency in all three counties for a winter storm with heavy snow, coastal flooding and strong winds.
State of Emergency for Sussex County and a Level 2 Driving Restriction for a winter storm with snow.
Statewide State of Emergency, effective March 21, for a winter storm with heavy snow in New Castle County and coastal flooding in Kent and Sussex counties.
State of Emergency for response and recovery from Tropical Storm Isaias (flooding, high winds and tornadoes).
State of Emergency in Kent and Sussex counties for a severe winter storm (blizzard).
State of Emergency for Hurricane Isabel, reported in place by September 18, 2003 alongside mandatory evacuations of low-lying areas.
Statewide State of Emergency, effective at midnight February 10, 2010, for the second February blizzard; WHYY reports it was declared once again after the first storm.

State of Emergency declared the morning of February 16, 2003 for the Presidents' Day winter storm with heavy snow, lifted at 6 a.m. on February 18 except in Wilmington (NOAA Storm Data, February 2003).

Extension of the COVID-19 Public Health Emergency order on September 8, 2021, in force during the remnants of Hurricane Ida (September 1 to 7, 2021) in New Castle County. It is a public health emergency, not a state of emergency (the COVID-19 state of emergency ended July 13, 2021), and none has been found for Ida itself, so it is a lesser declaration that matches DR-4627 only by date.
